item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #1 — Retailgentic: Caila Schwartz, Head of Agentic Commerce Salesforce is Back! Holiday 2026, State of Ecommerce, Plus... “The Caila Five”
item.ns1:encoded:
Score: 86/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

Originally published 27 Aug 2026

This episode is highly relevant, offering concrete data and predictions on agentic commerce, directly impacting a senior PM's focus on AI and eCommerce. The specific numbers, trends, and actionable predictions make it a must-listen for strategic planning.

Summary

Caila Schwartz, Salesforce's Head of Agentic Commerce Shopper Insights, provides a data-rich deep dive into the State of Commerce report and Holiday 2026 predictions. The episode highlights the dramatic increase in shoppers using LLMs and agents in their buying journeys, noting a 200% jump in those starting with an LLM/agent. It reveals that agentic search traffic converts at 2-3x higher rates than overall conversion and far above social commerce. Key predictions for Holiday 2026 include 20% non-human traffic, widespread deployment of branded agents, accelerated social commerce growth (9x faster than traditional e-commerce), the evolving hybrid role of physical stores, and the squeeze on free shipping. The discussion also touches on the 'referral blind spot' where discovery happens in conversations without direct clickbacks.

Key Ideas

  • 15% of shoppers now initiate their buying journey with an LLM or agent, a 200% increase from the previous spring, indicating a rapid shift in consumer behavior towards conversational commerce.
  • Agentic search traffic converts at 2.5-3.5%, which is 2-3 times higher than overall conversion rates and significantly outperforms social commerce's sub-1% conversion, highlighting the high intent and effectiveness of agent-assisted shopping.
  • Salesforce predicts that by Holiday 2026, 20% of e-commerce visits will originate from crawlers and agents (non-human traffic), and one in three e-commerce sites will have a branded agent deployed, signaling a critical need for brands to adapt their digital strategies.

Implications

Senior PMs in eCommerce must prioritize agentic commerce strategies, including developing branded agents, optimizing for conversational search, and understanding the new customer journey that may not involve traditional click-throughs. The data suggests a significant shift in traffic and conversion, requiring immediate strategic attention to remain competitive.

item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #2 — Jason & Scot Show: EP346 - Victoria's Secret & Co. EVP Digital, Brian Seewald
item.ns1:encoded:
Score: 82/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

Originally published 28 Aug 2026

The episode features a senior executive from a major retail brand discussing concrete digital transformation, AI applications in eCommerce, and strategic challenges like conversion rate definition and in-store vs. digital experiences. This directly aligns with the persona's focus on eCommerce, AI, and product strategy at a strategic depth.

Summary

Brian Seewald, EVP Digital at Victoria's Secret & Co., discusses the digital strategy behind the brand's turnaround. He shares his career path from traditional retail to e-commerce and delves into the complexities of defining conversion rates across varied traffic channels. The conversation highlights the success of VS and PINK apps, the evolution of 'PINK Wednesday Drops,' and the ongoing challenge of digital tools replacing the in-store bra-fitting experience. Seewald also outlines current AI and agentic commerce initiatives, including Google's UCP, TikTok Shop, and AI assistants for product pages, emphasizing the foundational PIM and content work required before implementing advanced AI solutions.

Key Ideas

  • Conversion rate definition needs to evolve beyond a simple metric when traffic quality varies wildly by channel, requiring a more nuanced understanding of channel-specific intent and customer journey.
  • Despite advancements in AI and virtual try-on, no digital bra-fitting tool has yet replicated the in-store experience, indicating a persistent gap in complex product categories where physical interaction remains critical for customer confidence and conversion.
  • Implementing AI and agentic commerce (e.g., AI assistants on PDPs, TikTok Shop integration) requires a robust, unglamorous foundation of PIM (Product Information Management) and content infrastructure, as 'we don't want a solution looking for a problem.'

Implications

This episode provides actionable insights for senior PMs in eCommerce, particularly regarding the strategic implementation of AI, the challenges of measuring digital performance accurately, and the enduring value of physical retail experiences for certain product categories. It underscores the importance of foundational data infrastructure for AI success.
